key_insight: Whole-brain MRI deep learning showed modest ability to predict HER2 status in breast cancer brain metastases, with a small numerical improvement from adding tumour masks.
clinical_relevance: This biomarker-prediction study—not drug discovery—explores a potential non-invasive complement to HER2 assessment but does not establish clinical readiness.
method: Analysed post-contrast T1-weighted brain MRI from 135 patients in the public BCBM-Radiogenomics dataset.
Compared conventional radiomics with a simple fully convolutional network.
Tested deep learning with MRI alone versus MRI plus expert-derived tumour masks.
evidence_signal: Among 70 HER2-positive and 65 HER2-negative patients, ROC-AUC was 0.602 for radiomics, 0.667 for MRI-only deep learning and 0.692 with tumour masks; the deep-learning confidence intervals overlapped.
watch_item: Modest discrimination and no external validation reported in the abstract limit conclusions about clinical use or the benefit of tumour masks.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
